name: Phil Wood Outboard Bottom Bracket - Sram GXP - aluminum / black
spec_notes: high-polish stainless steel or anodized aluminum cups
CNC-machined aluminum center sleeve w/ o-ring seals
use  Phil Wood OBB Tool  or  Park Tool BBT-19.2  for installation & removal
description:
Phil Wood manufactures their OBB cups, center sleeves and spacers for from US-produced 7075 aluminum and stainless steel, machined in-house at their facility in San Jose CA.
This version includes a genuine Phil Wood GXP adapter pressed into the non-drive side bearing, making it perfectly compatible with your Sram Omnium, Sram S300 or Alpina Track crankset.
Aluminum cups are available in 8 colors, stainless steel is polished silver.
ⓘ  Phil OBB cups are slightly thinner than stock Sram GXP bottom bracket cups, so it is important that you use one of the included 2.5mm spacers on the drive side for proper drive side clearance and left crank arm/axle engagement. Never use more than one of these spacers for GXP applications.

This bottom bracket includes two spacers that are only needed when installing a Sram wide axle MTB or CX crankset (which have longer spindles than Omnium, S300, and Sram's road cranksets) on a frame having a 68mm bottom bracket shell and 135mm rear spacing. Unless that's what you are doing, throw the spacers in the trash.

Spacers should never - we repeat  NEVER  - be used on Omnium or S300 cranksets to overcome clearance or chainline issues (regardless of the dumb stuff someone said on Reddit, what your kooky know-it-all friend told you or how the hack "mechanic" at your local shop does it).
This isn't just something we say to piss people off, and this information is also clearly noted on page 21 in Sram's crankset & bottom bracket tech documentation  here .

The axle can't somehow magically grow longer to accommodate the width of added spacers, so you will ruin the bearings and potentially damage the non drive-side crank arm axle interface if you use spacers.
